project.name: New Brand — AI + Human Points Concierge
project.status: brand name not yet finalised — placeholder mark used throughout
project.description: A worldwide points-to-Business-Class concierge built on a hybrid: fully manual human award search as the core product, an AI tool-search-plus-evaluation option for clients who want a wider net first (returns within a day), and a human alert service where a real person checks the client's programs daily and sends a report. The positioning is that both halves of the market are broken — automated tools return phantom seats, human desks are too slow — so we sell both and let the client pick the trade. No club model, no membership tiers copied from any competitor, no country-specific targeting, no founder-story section. Built from scratch as a distinct product with a distinct visual identity.
hard_constraints: No tier names resembling Explore / Platinum / Black or any other three-tier membership naming
No service named 'Points Flight Concierge' or close variants
No country-specific stats, currency defaults, or ABN/legal-entity footer language — site must read as global

No fabricated social proof (customer counts, dollar totals, review counts) — this is a new brand with no track record yet, trust has to come from the mechanism (human verification), not borrowed authority
No 'club', 'membership', or founder-narrative section anywhere in copy or navigation

brand.palette_verdict: Adopted the NUDE board (Davis Humphries). Supersedes the earlier cream tokens. Rich Romance was rejected before for its wine and dusty-rose tones; NUDE carries one comparable tone at #A48374, which is held OUT of the UI for that reason — see palette_notes.rose_withheld. The remaining five swatches map cleanly and are used exactly as given for surfaces.

palette_notes.text_tones_are_derived: Measured against #F1EDE6, only #3A2D28 clears WCAG for text (11.35:1). #A48374 is 2.96:1, #CBAD8D 1.82:1, #D1C7BD 1.43:1 — all unusable for copy. So ink_soft, ink_faint and accent_deep are derived in the same warm-brown family to stay legible: 5.62:1, 3.57:1 and 5.08:1 respectively. The board is a surface palette; it does not carry a readable mid-tone.
palette_notes.tan_is_decorative_only: #CBAD8D is 1.82:1 on canvas. It is the accent for underlines, the mark, rules and borders — never for text. Accent-coloured text uses accent_deep.
palette_notes.rose_withheld: #A48374 is defined but unused. It is the dusty-rose tone this project already rejected once as reading bridal/beauty. Say the word and it goes in; it fails text contrast either way, so it could only ever be a surface or decorative tone.

typography.display: Fraunces — used with restraint, headlines and section titles only
typography.utility_mono: IBM Plex Mono — labels, route codes, prices, data points

brand.logo: Placeholder geometric mark only until naming is finalised. Do not let a temporary wordmark ship to production.

animation_philosophy.summary: Alive and light, not dramatic and heavy. The old plan used pinned dark GSAP text reveals built for a moody premium brand — that toolset is wrong for a cream, quiet-luxury identity. Motion here should feel like breathing, not staging. Nothing pins the screen. Nothing is designed to feel weighty or urgent.
rules: Every animation must have a reason tied to content (a route drawing in, a number resolving, a card responding to hover) — no decorative motion with no informational job
All entrances under 0.6s, eased out, never bouncy or elastic — bounce reads playful-cheap, not alive-premium
Nothing loops indefinitely at a distracting speed — ambient motion should be slow enough to register as atmosphere, not animation

stagger_children.usage: Product pillar cards, FAQ items, process steps

route_line_draw.library: SVG stroke-dashoffset + GSAP ScrollTrigger or Framer Motion pathLength
route_line_draw.usage: A thin line traces a route between two points on a minimal world outline as the 'how it works' section scrolls into view — ties directly to the worldwide positioning without using a literal airplane icon

ambient_float.usage: One or two very low-opacity background shapes (a boarding-pass outline, a thin great-circle arc) drift a few pixels over 8-10s loops — background atmosphere only, never competes with foreground content

route_strip_marquee.usage: Horizontal scrolling strip of world city codes (carried over from the mockup) — keep, it already does the 'worldwide' job well

counter_reveal.usage: Only for real, concrete process facts (e.g. turnaround time, number of programs searched) — never for vanity metrics that don't exist yet

hover_card.underline_reveal: an accent-colored underline draws in under the card title on hover, left to right

eval_demo_interaction.usage: A small interactive teaser near the hero or 'how it works' section — user types or selects an example points balance, a result card animates in showing an example seat + savings. Makes 'AI-assisted' tangible instead of a claim in a sentence.
eval_demo_interaction.animation: input to result: fade-rise result card in 0.4s after a short 'searching' micro-state (skeleton pulse, not a spinner)

pages.note: No founder-story section per brief. Use this page to explain the verification mechanism and business model transparently instead — that's the trust asset for a brand with no track record yet.

sections.content_direction: The broken-system framing. Automated award search is fast and full of phantom seats; human award desks are accurate and slow. Both halves are broken, so we sell both and let the visitor choose the trade. Lead with the problem, not a vanity stat. Worldwide language, no region references. CTA drives to the free evaluation.

Three concrete steps: tell us what you hold -> choose your search (by hand: a person works it program by program and opens every booking; or AI-first: wider net, evaluation back within a day, machine-read and NOT human-confirmed) -> book the plan, or put the alert service on it. This section carries the trust weight that vanity stats would normally carry, so it must be specific and mechanical. State each mode's real trade-off; do not sell them as equally good.

cards.name: AI evaluation
cards.description: Tool searches wide across programs, an AI reads the results against the balance, back within a day. A machine read — explicitly NOT a confirmed seat. That distinction is the product line; never blur it.

cards.name: Manual search
cards.description: Fully manual. A person works the case by hand, program by program, opens each booking, confirms the seat is really there, and hands over a plan to act on.

cards.name: Human alert service
cards.description: A real person checks the client's specific programs every day and sends a report. Not an automated feed — someone actually looking, then writing.

sections.content_direction: Interactive, lightweight, makes the AI evaluation tangible. Not a full product demo, a teaser. Two things the copy must keep honest: the real evaluation takes a day (the preview is instant only because the data is pre-written), and nothing in it is human-confirmed — that is what the manual search adds.

Answer what a skeptical worldwide visitor actually asks: what a phantom seat is and why tools keep showing them, how this beats searching yourself, the difference between the free AI evaluation and the paid manual search, and whether the AI can be wrong. Answer that last one YES — the product is a choice between a fast machine read and a slow human one, and defending the AI would erase the distinction the manual search is sold on. Mechanism, never a promise with a number attached.

copy_rules: Active voice, plain verbs — 'we verify the seat,' not 'seat verification is performed'
No absolute guarantees with numbers attached (no '0% ghost flights', no '100% success rate') — describe the mechanism instead of promising an outcome
No borrowed vanity metrics — this is a new brand, say what's true today, not what a competitor says about itself
No region-specific currency, spend brackets, or legal-entity references — write for a reader who could be anywhere
Every button label states exactly what happens next, not a vague verb — 'Get my free evaluation,' not 'Get started'
notes_for_builder: Build homepage first with static copy and the entrance + hover animation layer only — get the palette and type system approved in context before adding the route-line-draw and ambient-float layers
The eval_demo interaction can be faked with static example data for now — no real seat.aero or AI call needed until the visual and motion are approved
Keep all animation timings and easing centralized in one file (animations.ts equivalent) so the 'alive but light' feel stays consistent across pages instead of drifting page to page
Do not reuse any component names, copy fragments, or asset files from the old iFlyFlat-clone project — start these files clean
